item.title: Ethics Training: Bring More Than One Person
item.description:
Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners

Greetings City of Columbus Partner,

Here is a practical suggestion:

Do not send just one person from your organization.

Send your board chair.

Send your executive director or CEO.

Send board members who regularly participate in City-related discussions.

Send anyone who helps your organization navigate governance, contracts, partnerships, or public-facing work.

Why? Because ethics questions are easier to manage when more than one person understands the framework. If only one person attends, that person becomes the unofficial “ethics translator” at the next board meeting.

That is a heavy job.

Also, nobody has ever said, “I wish fewer board members understood our obligations.”

On Monday, July 27, the City of Columbus is hosting an in-person training on Ohio Ethics Law and how it applies to nonprofit and private sector boards operating in the City’s orbit.

Event Details:

Date: Monday, July 27, 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm

Location: Continental Room at 1111 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43205

Speaker: Susan Willeke, Ohio Ethics Commission

Register here:

https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/019e179dca6d796e9e9688084b0f31a9

Please forward this to your full board and encourage them to register.

The best board discussions happen when everyone is working from the same map.

item.title: The Board Chair’s Invisible Job
item.description:
Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners

Greetings City of Columbus Partner,

Before your next board meeting, here are three questions worth asking:

  • Does our board include a City official or City employee serving in an official capacity?
  • Does our organization interact with, contract with, support, or receive support from the City?
  • Would our board know what to do if a conflict, disclosure, or public contract question came up?

If the answer to any of those is “yes,” “maybe,” or “I would rather not find out during a live board meeting,” this training is for you.

On Monday, July 27, the City of Columbus is hosting an in-person training on how Ohio Ethics Law applies to nonprofit and private sector boards operating in the City’s orbit.

This session will be led by Susan Willeke of the Ohio Ethics Commission.

The training will help board members and organizational leaders better understand the rules that may apply when public service and board service intersect.

Event Details:

Date: Monday, July 27, 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm

Location: Continental Room at 1111 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43205

Register here:

https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/019e179dca6d796e9e9688084b0f31a9

Please forward this to your board members.

A little clarity now can prevent a lot of confusion later.

item.title: The Board Chair’s Invisible Job
item.description:
Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners

Greetings City of Columbus Partner,

A good board chair does many things people notice.

They keep meetings moving. They make space for discussion. They help the board stay focused. They keep one person from turning a five-minute agenda item into a documentary series.

But some of the board chair’s most important work is invisible.

It is noticing when the board needs clarity.

Especially when the organization’s work overlaps with the City.

If your board includes a City official or City employee serving in an official capacity, your organization may face unique questions under Ohio Ethics Law.

What should board members know about conflicts of interest?

What happens when a board’s work involves City programs, City initiatives, or City contracts?

These are exactly the kinds of questions this training is designed to demystify.

Event Details:
Date: Monday, July 27, 2026
Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm
Location: Continental Room at 1111 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43205
Led by: Susan Willeke, Ohio Ethics Commission

Register here:

item.title: “Wait… can we vote on that?”
item.description:
Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners

Greetings City of Columbus Partner,

Every board has had some version of this moment.

The agenda is moving along.

Someone makes a motion.

A discussion begins.

Then someone pauses and asks:

“Wait… can we vote on that?”

And suddenly, the room gets very quiet.

For nonprofit boards connected to City work, that question can carry extra weight.

Especially when a City official or City employee serves on the board in their official capacity.

The issue may not always be obvious. It could involve a contract, a funding relationship, a disclosure issue, a conflict question, or simply uncertainty about what role someone is playing in that moment.

That is exactly why this training matters.

On Monday, July 27, the City of Columbus will host an in-person training led by Susan Willeke of the Ohio Ethics Commission to help nonprofit boards better understand how Ohio Ethics Law applies when public service and board service intersect.

It is for nonprofit executives, board chairs, board members, and organizational leaders who want to make informed decisions.

Event Details: Date: Monday, July 27, 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm

Location: Continental Room at 1111 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43205

Register here:

https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/019e179dca6d796e9e9688084b0f31a9

And yes, please forward this to your board.

Because “Wait… can we vote on that?” is a lot easier to answer when everyone has the same baseline understanding.

item.title: You’re Invited: Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners
item.description:
Ohio Ethics Law Training for City of Columbus Partners

Greetings City of Columbus Partner,

The City of Columbus is pleased to invite your organization to an in-person training on Ohio Ethics Law and how it applies to nonprofit boards and partner organizations operating in the City’s orbit.

This training is especially important for organizations where a City elected official, City official, City employee, or other public official serves on the board in their official capacity rather than as a private citizen.

The session will be led by Susan Willeke of the Ohio Ethics Commission and will cover important issues that may affect your organization, including conflicts of interest, disclosure obligations, public contracts, and related ethics requirements.

Nonprofit boards with City/Public officials serving in an official capacity may have unique ethical obligations that can affect the organization’s interactions and business with the City in ways that may not always be obvious.

This training is designed to help board members and organizational leaders better understand those requirements before questions arise in real time.

Event Details:

Date: Monday, July 27, 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm

Location: Continental Room at 1111 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43205

Please register here:

https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/019e179dca6d796e9e9688084b0f31a9

We encourage you to share this invitation with your full board and anyone in your organization who may benefit from this information.

A parking map with parking locations and the entrance door will be sent after registration.

We hope to see you there.

Please feel free to reach out to Renata Ramsini at RJRamsini@columbus.gov with any questions.

item.title: Reminder: Mandatory Cybersecurity Training Due June 30
item.description:
Mandatory Cybersecurity Training is Due by June 30

If you are receiving this message, our records show that as of June 26, you have not completed the mandatory 2026 City of Columbus Cybersecurity Essentials training. 

Cybersecurity is an important skill for work and personal safety while interacting online. As employees, we have required training each year, and the deadline is approaching!

All employees must complete this course  by Tuesday, June 30, by 5:00pm.

See below for the original announcement and full details.

-------- Original message from April 7, 2026 --------

 

Cybersecurity Training Required

In accordance with Ohio Revised Code section 9.64 (ORC §9.64), all local governments must establish cybersecurity training requirements for all employees of political subdivisions.

To establish and sustain compliance with this law, the Department of Technology (DOT) is partnering with Citywide Training to provide mandatory cybersecurity literacy training for all City employees.

The initial training consists of a series of short videos, typically a few minutes each, paired with an assessment. Additional training in the second half of 2026 will introduce role-based, specific scenarios, such as handling sensitive data or remote access.

The first courses will be assigned via the Training Gateway in April, with a completion target at the end of June.

Managers/HR Personnel:  

  • Alternate assignment options may be available. Contact Citywide Training (CTD@Columbus.gov or call 614-645-8294) to assist with your planning.
  • Group watch sessions are permissible. Schedule training events in your respective areas or reach out to Citywide Training to assist with planning. During the upcoming week, further information (instructions & sign-in sheets) will be available.

Why is this important?

Approximately 82% of successful data breaches involve human interaction. No cyber defense approach can effectively address cyber risk without a means to address people as a fundamental vulnerability.

It is tempting to think of cyber defense primarily as a technical challenge, but people's actions play a critical role in the success or failure of the City’s cybersecurity defenses. People fulfill important functions at every stage of system design, implementation, operation, use, and oversight.

Attackers know this and constantly attempt to exploit end users who may be susceptible to social engineering schemes such as phishing. They also seek environments where cybersecurity risks are not effectively understood, leaving executives and system owners with no reasonable way to make the investments necessary to mitigate them. Conversely, empowering people with good cyber defense habits can significantly increase readiness and reduce cybersecurity risk.

If you have any cybersecurity questions, reach out to DOT at TechDesk@Columbus.gov or call 614-645-5758.
